entries.title: Lens Intelligence (AI core)
entries.text: Lens Intelligence is the AI layer behind the command palette, the dock assistant, "send to AI" actions from the desktop and browser, and the MCP server. It is off by default . Until the user turns it on, nothing touches the network. - Providers - Built-in offline assistant ( script ) : a deterministic intent engine with no model and no network. It is also the mock provider for tests and CI. - Local model ( local ) : any OpenAI-compatible server on this PC (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp). - Claude ( claude ) : the Anthropic Messages API, using the user's own key. - Privacy : local only (the default), ask each time or allow cloud . - Tools : an allowlist of Lens's own actions, each with a risk level ( low , confirm or blocked ). The in-app assistant and the MCP server share the same registry. Code: src-tauri/src/ai/ (core), src-tauri/src/commands/ai.rs (commands), src/ai/contract.ts (types

entries.text: - local only : cloud providers are refused before any request is built. - ask each time : each cloud request asks first and names the context fields it would send. - allow cloud : cloud requests run without asking. - Context is only what the frontend attached. entries.title: Lens bridges: browser, right-click, links, scripts and Claude: The native host
entries.text: lens-ui.exe itself is the native-messaging host. Lens detects the launch from the arguments the browser passes: - Chromium browsers pass chrome-extension://<id / . - Firefox passes the manifest path and the extension id. The host manifests point straight at the exe, so no batch file or console window is involved. Protection is layered: 1. The browser only starts the host for ids listed in allowed origins / allowed extensions . 2. The host checks the caller again against the manifest Lens wrote. It also strips any path field, so a browser can never hand Lens a local file. 3. The host forwards each message over the loopback endpoint. Like the MCP bridge, the endpoint uses a random port and a 256-bit token, stored in %APPDATA%\LensUI\bridge-endpoint.json and compared in constant time. 4. The running Lens validates the message again: known fields only ( deny unknown fields ), known actions a

entries.title: Lens Command: Your own commands
entries.text: Add your own in %APPDATA%\LensUI\commands.json : a JSON array of templates. The same id overrides a built-in, and "enabled": false hides one. entries.text: Six families, all drawn in code from signed-distance shapes (no bitmaps are shipped): Family Idea --- --- Obsidian Monochrome body with a hairline rim, soft shadow. The Lens default. Accent Body filled with the theme pack's accent. Glass Frosted translucent body, white rim, dark outer line, wide soft shadow. Each family has a dark tone (dark body, light rim) and a light tone (light body, dark rim), plus a high-visibility option (thicker rim, opaque fill, a contrasting halo). Accent colours that would vanish against the body fall back to the rim colour. Every one of the 17 roles Windows uses is drawn: Arrow, Help, AppStarting,

entries.title: Cursor Suite: Applying
entries.text: apply cursor theme(style, size) : 1. Saves the user's current values to %APPDATA%\LensUI\cursors\backup.json unless a backup already exists (the first backup is the user's own setup and is never overwritten with Lens values). Saved: the scheme name (default value), all 17 role values (with their exact type, REG SZ or REG EXPAND SZ , and empty strings preserved), Scheme Source , CursorBaseSize , and whether Schemes\Lens UI existed. A corrupt backup is moved to backup.corrupt.json rather than trusted or overwritten. 2. Writes the 17 files to cursors\sets\<family -<tone [-hv]-<accent \ . 3. Writes HKCU\Control Panel\Cursors : the 17 paths as REG EXPAND SZ with %APPDATA% substituted back in, (Default) = Lens UI , Scheme Source = 1, CursorBaseSize (32–256, step 16; Windows 10 1903+), and a Schemes\Lens UI entry so the set also shows in Windows' Mouse Properties. 4. Calls SystemParametersInfoW

entries.title: Lens UI as an MCP server: How it works
entries.text: The AI app launches lens-ui.exe --mcp-stdio . With that flag Lens does not start the shell; the process is a thin bridge that forwards each JSON-RPC line to the running Lens UI and exits when stdin closes. While MCP is switched on, Lens UI listens on 127.0.0.1 on a random port and writes the port plus a random 256-bit token to %APPDATA%\LensUI\mcp-endpoint.json . Every connection must present the token first. Switching MCP off (or quitting) closes the port and deletes the file. If Lens UI is not running or MCP is off, the bridge still answers (so the AI app doesn't hang): every tool returns "Lens UI isn't running, or its MCP server is switched off". Why stdio + loopback instead of only HTTP: stdio is what every MCP client supports for local servers and needs no new crates; the loopback hop is plain std::net with no async runtime. All protocol logic is in src-tauri/src/win mcp.rs .

entries.title: Lens UI as an MCP server: Security model
entries.text: Off by default, loopback only, token-gated. The port binds to 127.0.0.1; a connection without the token from the endpoint file is closed before any message is read. The token file is in your user profile, so other programs running as you can read it — the same trust level as any app you run. No dangerous capabilities exist. There is no tool that runs commands or scripts, opens or deletes files, closes windows, kills processes, changes accounts or Windows settings beyond volume/brightness/night light. run action goes through the same router as Dock search and only after you click Approve. Validated input. Every argument is type- and range-checked (unknown tools are a protocol error); text is stripped of control characters and length-capped; window ids must belong to a window Lens currently lists. Rate-limited. 40 tool calls per minute per connection, 4 connections at once, 256 KB per mess

entries.title: Playground — living wallpapers: Desktop input (`win_desktop_input.rs`)
entries.text: The wallpaper never receives mouse input, so a low-level mouse hook forwards what happens over the bare desktop as lens://desktop-input events ( {kind, x, y, button, buttons, delta, alt, ctrl, shift} , x/y normalised 0..1 to the primary monitor). Never swallows input. The hook proc copies the event into a bounded channel with try send (dropped when full) and always returns CallNextHookEx . No window queries, no allocation, no locks in the hook proc. Desktop only. A worker thread checks WindowFromPoint : forwarded only when the window under the cursor is Progman / WorkerW / SHELLDLL DefView / SysListView32 (top-level Progman / WorkerW ) or the Lens wallpaper itself. entries.title: Lens UI Plugins
entries.text: Plugins are small HTML widgets for the Top Bar, the Dock and the Widget Drawer. They are off until you turn them on in Control Center → Plugins, and each one runs in a sealed sandbox: no internet, no files, no system access, only the permissions it lists.

entries.text: The entry file must be self-contained. Put CSS in <style and JS in <script ; images as data: URLs. External files, links, frames, forms, <base and <meta http-equiv are removed before the plugin runs.

entries.text: Permission What it allows :--- :--- (none) Time and theme colours only. telemetry Read CPU %, memory %, used/total GB, uptime. media Read the now-playing title, artist, album, app and artwork. storage Keep up to 64 values / 32 KB of its own data. notifications Show a Lens notification (title ≤ 80, body ≤ 200 chars, at most one per 10 s). launch-apps Start a Start-menu app by name — each app only after you approve it once . open-urls Open an https:// link in your browser — each site only after you approve it once . entries.title: Lens UI Plugins: Security model
entries.text: - Sandbox: <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc — an opaque origin: no cookies, storage, parent DOM, Tauri invoke() , popups, top navigation, forms, dialogs or downloads. Camera, microphone, clipboard, USB and similar features are denied with allow . - No network: a CSP at the top of every plugin document allows only inline script/style and data: images/fonts ( connect-src , frame-src , worker-src , object-src are 'none' ). WebRTC constructors are removed. The host window adds frame-src 'none' , so a plugin cannot navigate its own frame to a web page to carry data out in the URL. - Bridge: the only way out is postMessage . The host accepts messages only from that plugin's own frame, caps them at 16 KB, rate-limits to 20/s (burst 40), and stops a plugin after 50 violations. entries.title: Shelf and clipboard history — contract
entries.text: The Shelf is Lens's "standing clipboard": named collections of context items that stay until you remove them. Clipboard history v2 keeps what you copy (opt-in). Both are sealed on disk with DPAPI under %APPDATA%\LensUI and never leave the PC. Backend: src-tauri/src/shelf/ , src-tauri/src/clip/ , src-tauri/src/commands/{shelf,clip}.rs . Frontend types: src/shelf/contract.ts , src/clip/contract.ts . Other packages (browser bridge, AI surfaces, transcription) build against the Shelf contract below. Treat it as fixed.

entries.title: Lens UI — Shell Mode
entries.text: Shell Mode makes Lens UI the Windows shell for your user account : at sign-in Windows starts Lens UI instead of Explorer's desktop and taskbar. It is off by default and never required. Without it, Lens UI runs as an overlay on top of Explorer, exactly as before. Status: written but not yet run on a real machine. Try it on a spare account or a virtual machine first, and keep Restore-Windows-Shell.bat somewhere you can find it.

entries.title: Lens UI — Shell Mode: What it changes
entries.text: One registry value, for the current user only: Nothing machine-wide ( HKLM ) is ever written. Deleting that one value puts Windows back on Explorer. Other user accounts on the PC are not affected. Shell Mode can only be enabled from a release build. A development build ( bun run tauri dev ) refuses, because its program path is not stable.

entries.title: Lens UI — Shell Mode: Three ways back to the normal desktop
entries.text: 1. Restore-Windows-Shell.bat (in the Lens UI folder). Removes the registry value and starts Explorer. Works even if Lens UI will not start. 2. Task Manager. Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc → Run new task → type the full path to Restore-Windows-Shell.bat → OK. This keyboard shortcut works with no shell running at all. If you only type explorer there, you get a file window but not the taskbar, because Windows still thinks Lens is the shell — run the bat, or first run: reg delete "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v Shell /f and then explorer . 3. The automatic boot guard. Each time Lens starts as the shell it counts the attempt, and clears the count once the desktop has been up for about 20 seconds. If the next start finds the count still set, the previous one never reached a working desktop: Lens switches Shell Mode off, starts Explorer, and shows the reason in Control Cen

entries.title: Transcription (local, whisper.cpp)
entries.text: Lens turns audio and video into text on this PC. Nothing is uploaded. Pipeline: ffmpeg (any media → 16 kHz mono PCM WAV) → whisper-cli (whisper.cpp) → .txt , plus optional .srt subtitles. Where to start a transcription: - Settings › Transcription - Explorer › right-click a media file › Transcribe with Lens - the browser's Lens › Transcribe video - the transcribe file / transcribe url commands

entries.title: Transcription (local, whisper.cpp): Setting it up
entries.text: The card offers two routes. Lens never downloads anything silently. 1. Use your own tools. Point Lens at whisper-cli.exe and a ggml- .bin model. Lens also finds whisper-cli , ffmpeg and yt-dlp on PATH . A model dropped into %APPDATA%\LensUI\tools\whisper\ is picked up automatically. 2. Verified download (opt-in). The card lists every file before anything happens: its URL, approximate size, licence and destination. Nothing is fetched until you click Download . Each file must then match its pinned SHA-256 , or Lens deletes it. - Downloads use Windows' own curl.exe (HTTPS only, including redirects, with a size ceiling), and tar.exe unpacks the zip. - The checksums in media/setup.rs ( PINNED ) are still placeholders ( UNPINNED-… ). entries.title: Window styling 2.0: How it stays safe and reversible
entries.text: - No other process is modified for dimming, borders or peek. These effects are Lens' own native Win32 windows. They are click-through ( WS EX LAYERED WS EX TRANSPARENT ), never activate, and are not WebViews, so they cost almost no RAM. - The dim layer is one black layered window per monitor. It sits directly below the focused window, with a hole cut where that window is. - The border is four thin per-pixel-alpha strips directly above the focused window. Four strips use a fraction of the memory of one window drawn around the whole app. - Peek is a dark backdrop plus a live DWM thumbnail of the target, so the target window is never raised or recoloured. If the thumbnail fails, the backdrop gets a hole cut at the target instead. - Peek always ends on its own after a timeout (default 3 s, at most 10 s), so a missed mouse-out can never leave the screen dark. - Restore is hiding Lens' own win

lessons.title: First 5 minutes with Lens
lessons.summary: Find your way around: Settings, the dock, the top bar and how to get back to normal Windows.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.text: Lens keeps every option in one place: Settings (the Control Center). Open it from the gear in the dock or the top bar. The tabs on the left group everything by area.

steps.title: Look around the tabs
steps.text: Pick the Theme & Look tab. Every tab follows the same pattern: the main control first, then options below it.
steps.success: This is Theme & Look: theme at the top, options underneath.

steps.title: Find the dock
steps.text: The dock sits at the bottom of the screen. Click an app to open it, right-click it for more, and drag apps to reorder them.

steps.title: Try the palette
steps.text: Press Alt+Space to open the palette. Type an app, a file or a command like "dark mode".

steps.title: Know your escape hatch
steps.text: Everything Lens changes can be undone. If anything ever looks wrong, the Windows & Quick tab has a one-click restore, and Restore-Windows-Shell.bat in the Lens folder does the same from outside Lens.

lessons.title: Make it yours: themes, accents, dock and pointers
lessons.summary: Pick a theme pack, an accent colour, a dock style and a mouse pointer that fit together.

steps.title: Choose a theme pack
steps.text: The six recommended packs sit in one row. "Browse all" opens every pack with filters. A pack restyles surfaces, accents, icons, folders and window frames together.
steps.success: New look applied. You can always return with "Reset to" in the hero.

steps.title: Set an accent colour
steps.text: Click a swatch, or open the colour wheel for any colour. "Windows" follows your Windows accent instead.

steps.title: Pick a dock style
steps.text: Floating, Slim, Taskbar, Studio, Minimal or Split. Each keeps the same feel; Taskbar and Studio add a system area with the clock.

steps.title: Choose a mouse pointer
steps.text: Open "Mouse pointer" in Customise. Pick a family; it follows your accent colour. "Restore my Windows pointers" puts your old ones back exactly.

lessons.title: Windows like a pro
lessons.summary: Snapping, Alt+drag, hot corners, workspaces and summon keys.

steps.title: Snap and arrange
steps.text: In Lens Command type "snap left", "snap right" or "arrange windows". Windows' own Win+← and Win+→ still work too.

steps.title: Move windows with Alt+drag
steps.text: Turn on Alt+drag. Then hold Alt and drag anywhere inside a window to move it, or Alt+right-drag to resize. Full-screen and admin windows are left alone.

steps.title: Set a hot corner
steps.text: Give a screen corner an action, like Overview or Show desktop. Rest the pointer there to trigger it. Corners pause while a game or full-screen app is in front.

steps.title: Use workspaces
steps.text: Workspaces keep groups of windows apart. Switch with the workspace strip in Overview, or type "workspace 2" in Lens Command.

steps.title: Summon an app with one key
steps.text: Pick an app and a key. That key shows it, hides it, or launches it if it isn't running, like a drop-down terminal.

lessons.title: Your living desktop
lessons.summary: Playground scenes, click ripples, calm mode and idle mode.

steps.title: Pick a Playground scene
steps.text: Choose a scene in Desktops & Widgets › Living desktop. Falling Sand and Ink react to your pointer; Aurora, Rain on Glass and Starfield are calm.

steps.title: Paint on your desktop
steps.text: With Falling Sand, move to empty desktop and paint. Right-drag erases and the wheel changes the brush. If Windows' selection box gets in the way, switch the paint button to Alt + left or the middle button.

steps.title: One click to Calm
steps.text: Calm freezes the scene into a still picture and stops following the pointer. Scenes also pause on their own when a game or full-screen app is in front.

steps.title: Idle mode
steps.text: Idle mode shows a scene like a screensaver after a few minutes without input. It never starts over full-screen apps, games, presentations or calls.

lessons.title: Lens Command, Mini, Shelf and context packs
lessons.summary: One box for asking and doing, a pocket version, and a standing clipboard for context.

steps.title: Turn on Lens Command
steps.text: Lens Command is one input with modes: Ask, Do, Shelf, Clipboard and Actions. Tab cycles modes, "/" lists commands, "@" attaches context.

steps.title: Do something without AI
steps.text: Type "dark mode" or "volume 30". The script engine does it instantly, with no model and nothing sent anywhere.

steps.title: Open Lens Mini
steps.text: Tap the Command shortcut once for Mini next to your pointer; tap again for the full view. Mini's tiles change with the app you're in.

steps.title: Add things to the Shelf
steps.text: The Shelf keeps selections, pages, files and answers ready to use as context. Drag things onto the edge Shelf tab, or use "Add to Shelf" on any answer.

steps.title: Use the Shelf as context
steps.text: Type "@" in Command and pick Shelf items. The chips under the input show exactly what will be sent and where (Local or Claude). Remove any chip before sending.

lessons.title: Right-click everything
lessons.summary: The Lens menu in your browser and in File Explorer.

steps.title: Connect your browser
steps.text: Install the Lens browser extension, then use Install bridge in Settings › AI & Command › Connections. The extension never talks to the internet; it only talks to Lens on this PC.

steps.title: Right-click on a page
steps.text: Select text or right-click a page, link, image or video and open the Lens menu: Summarise, Explain, Translate, Rewrite, Extract, Add to Shelf, Copy as Markdown, Transcribe video.

steps.title: Add File Explorer actions
steps.text: Turn on File Explorer right-click for Ask, Summarise, Add to Shelf and Copy path into context. On Windows 11 they sit under "Show more options". Turning it off removes only what Lens added.

lessons.title: Voice control
lessons.summary: Say "Lens, minimise this" and more, with push-to-talk or a wake phrase.
lessons.requiresNote: Voice control isn't in this build yet. This lesson unlocks when it lands.

steps.title: Turn on voice
steps.text: Push-to-talk is the default. A wake phrase is optional and always shows a mic indicator while listening. Audio stays on this PC.

steps.title: Say a command
steps.text: Hold the push-to-talk key and say "minimise this" or "dark mode". The recognised command appears as a chip, with Undo when it can be undone.

steps.title: Ask a question
steps.text: Say "Lens, how do I change the dock style?". The Guide answers and offers "Show me".

lessons.title: Lens Browser and agent approvals
lessons.summary: How Lens asks before acting, in the browser and on the desktop.

steps.title: Approval cards
steps.text: When an AI proposes an action, Lens shows a card with what it will do, its risk, and Approve or Deny. Low-risk actions run straight away; anything that closes apps or changes settings asks first. Deleting, sending messages, spending money and credentials are always refused.

steps.title: Claude and other AI apps
steps.text: Claude Desktop and Claude Code can drive Lens through its MCP connection. They get the same approval cards. Turn the connection off any time in AI & Command.

steps.title: The browser side panel
steps.text: The extension's side panel streams answers and shows a Local or Claude badge plus exactly what was sent. The standalone Lens Browser adds tabs and agent approvals in its own window when it ships.

lessons.title: AI privacy explained
lessons.summary: What Lens AI can see, where it goes, and how to keep it all on this PC.

steps.title: AI is off until you turn it on
steps.text: Nothing AI-related runs until you enable it. The first engine is a script engine that needs no model at all.

steps.title: Choose an engine
steps.text: Script (instant, offline), a local model (Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp on this PC), or Claude with your own key stored encrypted on this PC.

steps.title: Pick a privacy mode
steps.text: Local only (the default) never sends anything off this PC. Ask each time shows exactly which context would be sent before it goes. Allow cloud sends without asking.

steps.title: See what was sent
steps.text: The usage log lists which engine answered, token counts and which kinds of context were attached. It never stores your prompts or answers.

lessons.title: Undo anything
lessons.summary: Every change Lens makes to Windows can be reversed.

steps.title: Back up your settings
steps.text: Save a backup of your Lens settings before big changes. Restore brings everything back in one click.

steps.title: Restore Windows' own look
steps.text: Pointers, window frames, the taskbar and Explorer right-click entries each have their own restore. Quitting Lens also reverts window styling and unpins anything Lens pinned.

steps.title: Remove all Lens changes
steps.text: "Remove all Lens changes" undoes every Windows change Lens made. Outside Lens, Restore-Windows-Shell.bat and Restore-Windows-Taskbar.bat do the same.

steps.title: Open things
steps.text: Alt+Space opens the palette. The Windows key opens the Lens Launcher when Shell keys are on. Ctrl+Alt+Space opens Lens Command (tap once for Mini).

steps.title: Windows
steps.text: Hold Alt and drag to move a window; Alt+right-drag to resize. In Overview, Shift+←/→ or Shift+1–9 moves the selected window to another workspace.

steps.title: Pointer and effects
steps.text: Ctrl+Shift+F8 toggles the pointer spotlight when pointer effects are on.

steps.title: Everywhere
steps.text: Esc always steps back one level. Ask the Guide "what's the shortcut for…" any time.
